title: Mohali: Aam Aadmi Clinic services may face disruption as support staff strike

ai.summary: Support staff at Aam Aadmi Clinics in Punjab are striking on November 25, risking service disruptions for patients, as they demand regularisation of services, higher incentives, and insurance cover.

facts.claim: Support staff at Aam Aadmi Clinics in Punjab are striking on November 25
facts.quote: Patients visiting Aam Aadmi Clinics across Punjab may face delays and disruption as pharmacy officers, doctors and clinical assistants will stay away from work amid a state-wide protest on November 25.

facts.claim: The strike affects pharmacy officers, doctors and clinical assistants
facts.quote: With pharmacy officers and clinical assistants absent, doctors are likely to shoulder additional responsibilities, including patient consultations and examinations.

facts.claim: The strike demands include regularisation of services, higher incentives and insurance cover for employees
facts.quote: The Aam Aadmi Clinics Sanjha Front has called a protest and hunger strike over demands that include regularisation of services, higher incentives and insurance cover for employees.

facts.claim: The employees claim their demands have received in-principle approval but no formal orders
facts.quote: They claimed their demands had received in-principle approval, but no formal orders had been issued.

facts.claim: The front is seeking separate incentives for national health programmes, full payment for Sundays and public holidays, and a minimum payment equivalent to 75 patients a day
facts.quote: Apart from regularisation, the front is seeking separate incentives for national health programmes, full payment for Sundays and public holidays, and a minimum payment equivalent to 75 patients a day, irrespective of actual OPD attendance.

ai.background_note: The Aam Aadmi Clinics Sanjha Front is a group of support staff at Aam Aadmi Clinics in Punjab who are striking for better conditions and regularisation of services.
